subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence :
stem: Louvre Museum has in its collection the much acclaimed painting of ____ by Leonardo-da-Vinci.
solution:
**(B)** Mona Lisa
Louvre Museum has in its collection the much acclaimed painting of Mona Lisa by Leonardo-da-Vinci. The Louvre Museum in Paris was established in the 18th century C.E. to exhibit the antiquities collected by members of the French royal family. Leonardo da Vinci, the world renowned artist, worked under the patronage of Francis I, the king of France, in the 16th century. Napoleon Bonaparte only added to the Louvre collection the antiquities brought back from his conquests, while Sir Hans Sloan and King George II are connected with the British Museum in London.

subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence :
stem: ____ is supposed to be the first Keertankar in Maharashtra.
solution:
**(C)** Saint Namdev
Saint Namdev is supposed to be the first Keertankar in Maharashtra. Traditionally, Naradmuni is regarded as the founder of the Keertan tradition, and in Maharashtra Saint Namadev is known as the first keertankar; other saints later helped the tradition to flourish. A keertankar is also known as Haridas or Kathekaribuva.

subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence :
stem: The book ____ written by Hegel is well known.
solution:
**(B)** Reason in History
The book 'Reason in History' written by Hegel is well known. Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel convinced many scholars that historical methods were not of lesser quality than scientific methods, though they differed from them. The other titles belong to other scholars: 'The Secret of World History' is a collection of Leopold von Ranke's articles, 'Archaeology of Knowledge' was written by Michel Foucault and 'Discourse on the Method' by Rene Descartes.

context: Identify the wrong pair in the following and rewrite :

(iv) Chess — Outdoor game

subject: History
context: Write short notes on (any two) :
stem: Write a short note on : Vishwakosh.
solution:
A Vishwakosh is a comprehensive encyclopaedia. An encyclopaedia is a systematic compilation of information or knowledge on various topics, arranged by a specified method, and its main objective is to organise available knowledge and make it accessible.
(1) There are two types of Vishwakosh. One type includes all subjects under the sun, for example 'Encyclopaedia Britannica', 'Maharashtriya Dnyankosh' and 'Marathi Vishvakosh'. The other type gives comprehensive information on one chosen subject, for example 'Bharatiya Samskruti Kosh' and 'Vyayam Dnyankosh'.
(2) Its articles are written by subject experts, under a single editor or an editorial committee, and are arranged either alphabetically or by topics, with an index at the end.
(3) Accuracy, objectivity, a standardised format and updated information are its criteria, so revised editions or supplements are published from time to time.
(4) Twenty three volumes of 'Maharashtriya Dnyankosh' edited by Shridhar Vyankatesh Ketkar are available; his aim was to widen access to knowledge for Marathi speaking people.

subject: History
context: Write short notes on (any two) :
stem: Write a short note on : Applied History.
solution:
(1) 'Applied History' is also known as 'Public History'. It is a field of study concerned with the application of history for the benefit of people in contemporary and future times.
(2) Knowledge of history can guide us in finding solutions to contemporary social issues and in incorporating them in social planning.
(3) Projects and programmes of applied history create opportunities for people to participate along with technical experts: as tourists visiting museums and ancient sites, or as volunteers in the conservation and preservation projects of their own city, town or village.
(4) Public history removes the misgiving that history has no practical use, and connects people with history in everyday life. The method of history is also of value in research in fields like philosophy, science, technology, industry and commerce, management, arts and the humanities.
(5) Many universities abroad offer courses in public history, and the Srushti Institute of Art Design and Technology at Bengaluru has a separate 'Centre for Public History'.

subject: History
context: Write short notes on (any two) :
stem: Write a short note on : Mass Media and Professional Opportunities.
solution:
(1) Newspapers have to give fresh news and also unfold the background of an event. Reporters compare the news with parallel events of the past, and newspapers print columns like '50 Years Ago' or '100 Years Ago', supplements and special issues on anniversaries such as the 75 years of the 'Quit India' movement. All these writings need a knowledge of history.
(2) History is essential in planning radio programmes. Akashvani invites historians as experts for discussions on the anniversaries of national leaders and historical events, and broadcasts programmes like 'On This Day in History'.
(3) Television channels such as Doordarshan, 'Discovery', 'National Geographic' and 'History' telecast historical serials and shows. Producing them needs a deep understanding of the period, so that environment, outfits, weaponry, life styles and language are presented accurately.
(4) Thus people with a deep knowledge of history are sought out in newspapers, radio and television, and students of history find many professional opportunities in mass media.

subject: History
subtopic: Sources of History, their Conservation and Preservation
context: Explain the following sentences with reasons (any two) :
stem: Only trained persons who are duly qualified can take up the tasks involved in the work of preservation and conservation.
solution: Every step in this work, collecting the sources of history, creating their records and indexes, and exhibiting manuscripts, old books and artefacts after the necessary treatments, requires very careful handling and management. Written sources have to go through mechanical and chemical processes of cleaning, and their historical value has to be ascertained. This needs specific skills, such as knowledge of scripts like Brahmi, Modi and Persian, of the types of paper, ink and colours, of the properties of the stones and metals used for inscriptions, and of the equipment and chemicals used in cleaning, conservation and preservation. Hence only trained persons who are duly qualified can take up these tasks.

subject: History
context: Explain the following sentences with reasons (any two) :
stem: Historical research was driven to focus in depth on various aspects of women's life.
solution: Feminist historiography means the restructuring of history from the perspective of women. The writings of Simone de Beauvoir helped in establishing the fundamentals of feminism. Feminist historiography emphasised not only the inclusion of women in history but also the rethinking of the male dominated perspective of history. Therefore historical research was driven to focus in depth on various aspects of women's life, such as their employment, their role in trade unions, the institutions working for their cause and their family life. In the historical writings after 1990, women were portrayed as an independent social class.

subject: History
context: Explain the following sentences with reasons (any two) :
stem: Bakhar is an important type of historical documents.
solution: A bakhar is a historical document of medieval times. It contains eulogies of heroes and stories of historic events, battles and the lives of great men. For example, 'Sabhasad Bakhar', written by Krishnaji Anant Sabhasad during the reign of Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj, is important for information about the rule of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, and 'Bhausahebanchi Bakhar' describes the Battle of Panipat. Bakhars are of various types, such as biographies of kings, dynastic histories, descriptions of events and histories of sects. Hence a bakhar is an important type of historical document.

subject: History
context: Explain the following sentences with reasons (any two) :
stem: We need mass media to facilitate free flow of information to all strata of the society.
solution: Mass media are the modes of communication through which information reaches a large aggregation of people at the same time. Newspapers carry local, national and international news along with editorials, columns and supplements, and give readers a platform to voice their opinions, which helps to make democracy stronger. Radio reaches every section of society: Akashvani broadcasts special programmes for farmers, workers, the youth and women, and 'Vividh Bharati' is broadcast in 24 regional languages and 146 dialects. Television, an audio-visual medium, crosses the limitations of newspapers and radio by showing the actual visuals of an event. Hence we need mass media for the free flow of information to all strata of society.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: What is Marxist history ?
solution:
(1) Marxist history is based on the thesis of Karl Marx (1818-1883). According to Marx, history is not about abstract ideas; it is about living people. Human relationships are shaped by the fundamental needs of people and by the ownership and nature of the means of production used to meet those needs.
(2) The access of different strata of society to these means is not equal. This inequality divides society into classes and leads to class struggle. According to Marx, human history is the history of class struggle, because the class that owns the means of production economically exploits the other classes. His treatise 'Das Kapital' is the most referred book all over the world.
(3) In Marxist historiography, the means of production, the modes of production and industrial relations are at the centre, and analysing the impact of every significant social event is its basic theme.
(4) Marxist historians in India studied the transitions within the caste system. Scholars like Damodar Dharmanand Kosambi, Comrade Shripad Amrut Dange, Ram Sharan Sharma and Comrade Sharad Patil contributed notably. Comrade Dange, a founder member of the Indian Communist Party, wrote 'Primitive Communism to Slavery', which represents Marxist historiography.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: Write information about Dashavatara Theatre in Maharashtra.
solution:
(1) Dashavatara is a part of the folk theatre of Maharashtra. Its shows are presented in the Konkan and Goa regions after the harvesting season is over.
(2) The stories presented are based on the ten incarnations of Vishnu: Matsya, Koorma, Varaha, Narsimha, Wamana, Parashurama, Ram, Krishna, Buddha and Kalki.
(3) At the beginning of the show the sutradhara, the narrator, invokes Lord Ganesha, the destroyer of obstacles.
(4) The method of acting, the make-up and the costumes are set by tradition. The show is mostly musical, with a few spontaneous dialogues, and the characters representing gods wear wooden masks. The show ends with the breaking of the dahihandi, an earthen pot of curds, followed by the aarati.
(5) In the 18th century Shyamji Naik Kale started a phad (troupe) of Dashavatara artists which performed all over Maharashtra. Vishnudas Bhave, the pioneer of Marathi theatre, staged mythological plays by modifying the Dashavatara style, so the origins of Marathi theatre can be traced to the Dashavatara tradition.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: Explain the close tie between sports and history.
solution:
Although sports and history appear to be distant subjects, there is a close tie between them.
(1) To play is a natural human instinct, so the history of sports begins with the origin of mankind. Ancient Indian literature and the epics mention games like dice, wrestling, horse and chariot races and chess, and toys found in excavations throw light on cultural history and on contacts between nations.
(2) Students of history find many opportunities in sports journalism, because writing articles and reviews about events like the Olympics, the Asiad and national and international matches needs a knowledge of history.
(3) An expert commentator must know the history, statistics, previous records, eminent players and historical anecdotes of the game. Bal J. Pandit's cricket commentaries on Akashvani were popular because of such historical details.
(4) Knowledge of the history of sports is needed for writing in encyclopaedias, newspapers and sports magazines, and for making films on sports and on the lives of players, which require a deep study of the period, its language, dress and social life.
Thus history is useful in many fields connected with sports.

subject: History
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: Write the history of Akashvani.
solution:
(1) The 'Indian Broadcasting Company' (IBC), a private radio company, was the first to broadcast daily programmes in India.
(2) Later the British Government took over the company and named it the 'Indian State Broadcasting Service' (ISBS). On 8th June 1936 it was renamed 'All India Radio' (AIR).
(3) After independence, AIR became an integral part of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. In the beginning it broadcast governmental programmes and schemes. It was named 'Akashvani' on the suggestion of the famous poet Pandit Narendra Sharma.
(4) Akashvani broadcasts entertainment, awareness creating and literary programmes, and special programmes for farmers, workers, the youth and women. Its 'Vividh Bharati' programmes are broadcast in 24 regional languages and 146 dialects.
(5) Akashvani has preserved recordings of all the speeches delivered by the prime ministers of India on 15th August, invites historians for discussions on historical anniversaries, and broadcasts 'On This Day in History' daily. Lately new channels like 'Radio Mirchi' also provide radio services.

subject: Political Science
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentences :
stem: The Voters age decided by the Indian Constitution is ____ .
solution:
**(C)** 18
The Voters age decided by the Indian Constitution is 18. The Constitution first gave the right to vote equally to men and women above the age of 21 years; the voting age was later reduced from 21 to 18, which gave the young generation an opportunity of political participation. Today every Indian citizen who has completed 18 years of age has the right to vote.

subject: Political Science
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentences :
stem: Santhal and Munda from ____ started uprising on a large scale.
solution:
**(D)** Bihar
Santhal and Munda from Bihar started uprising on a large scale. In the pre-independence period the British government deprived tribal people of their right to livelihood on forest resources, which led to tribal uprisings: the Kolam from Chota Nagpur, the Gond from Orissa, the Koli, Bhilla and Ramoshi from Maharashtra, and the Santhal and Munda from Bihar.

subject: Political Science
subtopic: Characteristics and Functions of Political Parties
context: State whether the following statements are true or false. Give reasons for your answer (any two) :
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give the reason for your answer : Political Parties act as a link between government and people.
solution: True. Acting as a link between the government and the people is an important characteristic of political parties. Political parties communicate the demands and complaints of the people to the government. In turn, the government tries to get the support of the people for its policies and programmes through political parties. In this way parties connect common people with democracy, representation and elections.

subject: Political Science
context: State whether the following statements are true or false. Give reasons for your answer (any two) :
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give the reason for your answer : Importance of the problems of farmers and tribals has increased in the left extremist movement.
solution: False. Naxalism, the left extremist movement, began as a movement to remove injustice against landless farmers and tribal people. But today it has become a violent struggle. In the Naxalite movement the importance of the problems of farmers and tribal people has reduced; instead, Naxalite groups use violent measures to oppose government policies and attack the police forces. Hence left extremism is a major challenge before Indian democracy.

subject: Political Science
context: State whether the following statements are true or false. Give reasons for your answer (any two) :
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give the reason for your answer : In the post-independence period efforts were made for empowering women.
solution: True. Taking the problems of women into consideration, several policies were adopted after independence to remove illiteracy among women and to give them opportunities for development. Laws like the right to an equal share in the property of the father and husband, the Dowry Prohibition Act, the act against sexual harassment and the Domestic Violence Prohibition Act protect the freedom of women. To increase their political representation, the 73rd and 74th amendments reserved 33% of seats for women in local self-governing institutions, and this has been raised to 50% in several states including Maharashtra.

subject: Political Science
context: Explain the following concepts (any one) :
stem: Explain the following concept : Right to Information.
solution: Citizen empowerment is the essential condition of democracy, and citizens have a right to know about the functioning of the government. The Government of India gave citizens the Right to Information (RTI, 2005) to ensure transparency and accountability, which are the hallmarks of good governance. The Right to Information has made the government more transparent and has reduced secrecy in its working. It increases communication between citizens and the government, builds a relationship of trust between them and thus strengthens democracy.

subject: Political Science
context: Explain the following concepts (any one) :
stem: Explain the following concept : Corruption.
solution: Corruption is a major challenge before Indian democracy; its extent is said to be very high in the public sector. Corruption at the political and administrative levels reduces the working capacity of the government. Delay in government work, poor public services and financial blunders make people distrust and feel dissatisfied with the whole system. Corruption in the electoral process, such as bogus voting and bribing or abducting voters, reduces people's confidence in the democratic process.

subject: Political Science
context: Answer the following questions in brief (any one) :
stem: Write some additional information about the post of the Election Commissioner.
solution:
(1) The Election Commission, established by Art. 324 of the Indian Constitution, is an autonomous body consisting of one Chief Election Commissioner and two other commissioners.
(2) The President appoints the election commissioners.
(3) The Chief Election Commissioner cannot be removed from his post easily or on account of any political reasons. This is necessary to preserve the independence of the Election Commission, and a separate provision is made for its expenses.
(4) The Commission has no separate staff; government officers, teachers and other employees help it to conduct elections.
(5) Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner after independence. He took charge after the Election Commission was established in 1950 and handled the responsibility efficiently in extremely adverse conditions.

subject: Political Science
context: Answer the following questions in brief (any one) :
stem: Explain the functions of environmental movement.
solution:
Environmental degradation is a serious problem at the national and international level, and environmental movements work to stop the deterioration of the environment. Their functions are:
(1) To take up issues like the protection of bio-diversity, the protection of different sources of water and of forests, the green belt, the pollution of rivers, and the use of chemicals and their ill effects.
(2) To organise people on these issues, build public opinion about them and thereby put pressure on political parties and the government to resolve them.
(3) To give the government necessary information about these issues, which is useful while making policies.
(4) At the international level, several movements work together, and there is significant international cooperation in this field.
